learning_objective: 🎯 You will learn how to add exciting details to your action words by discovering how, when, and where things happen!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An adverb is a describing word, but instead of describing things, it describes actions (verbs)! It tells us more about a verb, an adjective, or even another adverb. It answers questions like How? When? or Where?
These adverbs tell us exactly HOW an action is done. Most of them end in '-ly'. For example, if you ask 'How does he run?', the adverb answers: 'He runs QUICKLY' or 'He runs SLOWLY'.
Want to know WHEN something happened? Use an adverb of time! Words like 'today', 'tomorrow', 'now', 'never', and 'always' tell us the time of the action.
These adverbs tell us WHERE the action is taking place. Words like 'here', 'there', 'everywhere', 'inside', and 'outside' act as adverbs of place.

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Robot Action Game
fun_activity.instructions: Walk across the room in three different ways. Write down a sentence for each using adverbs of manner, like 'I walked slowly,' 'I walked noisily,' and 'I walked cheerfully!'

quick_recap: ⭐ Adverbs add extra meaning to verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
⭐ Adverbs of Manner tell us HOW an action happens.
⭐ Adverbs of Time tell us WHEN an action happens.
⭐ Adverbs of Place tell us WHERE an action happens.
